note: The message-to-document case study (lib/casestudy.mjs): the message, what its analysis finds, the questions and their answers, the editorial decisions, and where each fact of the message lands in reset-mfa.md. The message and the answers were written for this portfolio.

parts: call the number in the HR system
don't trust the one in the ticket
aside: can someone please write this down properly. third time this month i've explained it

facts.find: Confirm that the request is genuine.
Call the user on the number in the HR system
not the number in the ticket
Contractor accounts follow a different process
reassign those tickets to the IAM team
find the user and open their profile
It leaves the old phone enrolled.
open the enrollment email and enroll the new phone
the user's sign-in log shows a new MFA enrollment

analysis.label: Requirement
analysis.text: Clear the user's MFA, so that they can enroll a new phone.

analysis.label: Precondition
analysis.quote: make sure it's actually them first
analysis.text: The caller is confirmed as the user before anything changes.

analysis.label: Risk
analysis.text: The button that looks right leaves the old phone enrolled.

analysis.label: Dependency
analysis.text: Contractor accounts belong to the IAM team, not to the service desk.

analysis.label: Missing
analysis.text: Which log, and what it shows when the reset worked.

analysis.label: Ambiguous
analysis.text: Locked out by a lost phone, or by a forgotten password?

questions.q: Locked out how: by a lost or replaced phone only, or by a forgotten password too?
questions.a: Only a lost or replaced phone. A forgotten password has its own procedure.

questions.q: Which log shows that the reset worked, and what does it show?
questions.a: The user's sign-in log in the admin console: a new MFA enrollment, dated today.

questions.q: How does a contractor's request reach the IAM team?
questions.a: Reassign the ticket to the IAM team.

questions.q: What if the enrollment email doesn't reach the user?
questions.a: Reassign the ticket to the IAM team as well. They have other ways to confirm a user.

decisions.t: The title names the task and who it's for.
decisions.why: A reader searching for “MFA” or “locked out” finds it, and knows from the title whether it's theirs.

decisions.t: The identity check comes before the first step.
decisions.why: In the message it came near the end, with “first” as its only signal. A reader who follows the order would reset first and check after.

decisions.t: “NOT reset password” becomes a caution on the step it concerns.
decisions.why: The warning sits where the wrong button is, and keeps the message's reason: the old phone stays enrolled.

decisions.t: Contractors become a scope rule before the steps.
decisions.why: Nobody starts a procedure that doesn't cover their account, and the rule says where those tickets go (answer 3).

decisions.t: “check the log after” becomes a result the reader can verify.
decisions.why: It names the log and what it shows (answer 2). A check that says only “check the log” can't fail.
The greeting, the emphasis and the complaint carry no instruction. “Third time this month” is the reason to write the document, not a part of it.

sources.s: Select Reset MFA, not Reset password.
Reset password leaves the old phone enrolled.
The user gets an enrollment email.
Call the number in the HR system, not the number in the ticket.
The procedure is for a lost or replaced phone.
The sign-in log shows a new MFA enrollment, dated today.
Contractor tickets, and users the email doesn't reach, go to the IAM team.

sources.status: Removed: the message gives no time, and nobody has measured it

terms.rule: Spelled out once, as “multi-factor authentication (MFA)”, then MFA.
The one verb for adding a phone, as the message has it. Not “register”.
The message's word for the second factor. Not “device”, which could be a laptop.
As the message names it, in lowercase, because it names a kind of console, not a product.
For a button. Not “click” or “hit”, which assume a mouse.

review: The identity team checks steps 1 to 3, the caution and the result against the admin console. It hasn't happened: this is a demonstration, and no team has reviewed it.
